version.author: Magnolius
version.changelog:
Two releases' worth of work: 1.3 was never published, so this carries its interface as well.
NEW INTERFACE, built on the Magnolius GUI kit: knobs and typed value fields for every parameter, a decay view of the loaded IR with the pre-delay drawn on it, a built-in help panel and an interface scale. The IR browser is unchanged. The Reverb IR file slider stays visible in REAPER's parameter list, since only the host can drive a file slider. The IR length cap also goes up from 5.5 s to 8.2 s at 48 kHz (128 to 192 partitions), which fits in the memory already reserved and costs no extra CPU unless you actually load a longer IR.
Fixes a long-standing bug in the IR browser: the file list ignored the mouse wheel until a row had been clicked, because the keep-the-selection- visible clamp ran every frame and undid the scroll on the next one.
LATE-TAIL MODULATION. A convolution reverb is a fixed filter, so its tail is frozen - the same comb structure on every note, which on sustained material reads as a static, glassy quality that algorithmic hardware does not have. Three new controls (Depth, Rate, Onset) add slow movement to the tail ONLY, leaving the early reflections that carry source position and room identity untouched.
Where "late" begins is measured per IR rather than fixed: an Abel-Huang echo-density profile finds the mixing time, which runs from ~10 ms in a small room to 150 ms in a cathedral. It converged on all 134 IRs of the Samplicity M7 set. The split is made in the IR itself, not on a partition boundary, so the detection is not quantised to 42.7 ms steps.
Depth at 0 is bit-identical to the unmodulated engine and costs no CPU; the whole feature costs about 10% with it on. Modulation switches itself off for IRs under half a second, which also keeps cabinet impulses and correction curves out of it. It is deterministic, so a project bounces the same way twice.
Depth ships at a low setting rather than Off, so the improvement is audible on first load.
Also fixes a pre-delay bug that predates both: the crossfade that hides a pre-delay change never ran, because EEL2 identifiers are case-insensitive and the pre_xf countdown was the same variable as the PRE_XF constant. A pre-delay change moved the read tap outright, pitch-shifting the tail.
The window grows to 958 px wide to fit the modulation panel; the browser and the decay view take the extra width with it.

version.author: Magnolius
version.changelog:
New interface built on the Magnolius GUI kit: knobs with typed value fields, the scrolling display in a framed plot with the lift overlaid on it, the live transfer curve as a panel, a scale selector shared with the other Magnolius plugins, and a built-in help panel.
Range now stops at 12 dB instead of 40, and the lift overlay is drawn on a fixed 0-12 dB scale rather than one that followed Range - on the old scale, raising Range made the same lift draw shorter. A project saved with Range above 12 loads clamped to 12.

version.author: Magnolius
version.changelog:
New interface built on the Magnolius GUI kit: knobs with typed value fields, the scrolling display in a framed plot, a live transfer curve that bends as the ratio solves, GR and ratio meters, a scale selector shared with the other Magnolius plugins, and a built-in help panel.
The scrolling display now plots dB rather than linear amplitude, with the threshold and the ceiling drawn on it as real reference lines. On the old linear scale everything below about -30 dB was a hairline on the centre line, which is most of what a threshold down at -60 is actually working on.
New Display History control (1-30 s) for the scroll window, which used to be hardwired to about 5 s.
Max Ratio now runs 1:1 to 10:1 in steps of 0.1, instead of 2:1 to 1000:1 in steps of 1. On the old range the musically useful part of the control lived in the first few per cent of its travel, which a knob makes far worse than a slider did, and the old floor of 2:1 ruled out the gentle ratios this compressor is often wanted for. 1:1 is a valid setting: it pins the solver at unity, so the compression is off while Blend and Output Gain still work.
A project saved with Max Ratio above 10 loads clamped to 10, which will compress less than it used to - raise the threshold or lower the ceiling to compensate.
The default moves from 200 to 3. The old default was chosen to be out of the way - at 200:1 the clamp effectively never engaged and the ceiling was always held by the ratio. 3:1 is a real setting rather than a disabled one, so a new instance now sounds like a compressor from the first note. Raise it towards 10:1 for the old behaviour. Existing projects keep their own saved value; only new instances see this.
Simplified: the safety clipper, the Safety Clip switch, the Makeup Position switch and the Out Peak readout are all gone.
The ratio trace and the RATIO meter are now on a FIXED 1:1 to 10:1 scale instead of one that followed Max Ratio. Following it meant the same ratio drew at a different height as Max Ratio moved, which reads as the ratio having changed when nothing about the audio did - the same reason the gain-reduction overlay has always been pinned to 0-24 dB.
Their slider NUMBERS (6 and 10) are left as gaps rather than renumbering the rest down. A project stores slider values positionally by slider number, so this keeps every remaining control loading into itself. REAPER does however compact the PARAMETER indices it exposes to automation, so an existing envelope on Lookahead, Ratio Release, Max Ratio or Display History now points one parameter too high and needs re-pointing. That is unavoidable when a parameter is removed - the gaps do not change it.
Output Gain (was Makeup Gain) is now ALWAYS applied last, after the blend, and is no longer part of the ratio solve. The old Pre position folded it into the solve so the compressor worked harder to hold the ceiling despite it; that behaviour no longer exists. A project saved in Pre will now be louder and less compressed than it was - it now behaves as if it had been saved in Post, which was the default.
Without the clipper, Output Ceiling is no longer an absolute guarantee. It is hit exactly while the required ratio is within Max Ratio, and peaks pass once the ratio is capped - which the new 3:1 default makes an everyday case, not a rare one. Put a limiter after this if you need a true ceiling.
Input Gain is unchanged, and remains a genuine pre-compressor drive: the detector, the curve and the dry half of the blend all see it.
Alt-drag on Input Gain or Output Gain moves the other one the opposite way by the same number of dB, so you can change how hard the compressor works without changing the level. It works on the knob, the wheel and the value field, and each value still clamps to its own range.
